notes: Golden scenarios for the N02 control channel (bead ffw-ugf). Each `expect` was worked out by hand from docs/contracts/n02.md before any implementation produced it.

They are replayed by tests/n02/reference.py (an independently structured model) and by the Rust channel (crates/franken-control, test `replay`). A disagreement between any two of the three is a finding.
Start state of every scenario: group epoch 10, state revision 2, members kitchen and den at volume 50 and unmuted, group master volume 50, nothing stopped.
Peers: ctl-a and ctl-b (remote controllers, keys bound to epoch 10), panel (the local user, not epoch-bound), rogue (a remote controller whose key is bound to epoch 900).
Times are in milliseconds. A rate limit [burst, interval_ms] allows `burst` actions at once and one more per interval.
These are host-simulation vectors for a message-handling state machine. They say nothing about a network, a real MAC, or a board.

signing_vectors.what: relative member volume with an expected revision (also pinned by a hand-written Rust unit test)
absolute group volume at the top of the range, with an expected revision

scenarios.title: the acknowledgement is lost after the commit; the retry gets the recorded outcome and nothing is applied twice
a duplicate relative volume produces one effect whether the copy arrives before or after the command is applied
after the retention window a retry is explicitly unknown and is not applied again
a full ledger forgets its oldest outcome and says so; newer ones are still answered
a stale leader cannot alter a group whose epoch has moved on; rebinding its key to the new epoch restores it
a key bound to one epoch is refused under another, and an epoch jump from a peer bound to one is refused and never fences the group
two controllers read the same revision; only the first relative change applies and the second is refused
the same command number with different content is refused, while waiting and after it settled
the ordinary queue is bounded; a copy of a waiting command is still answered; a refused number is not consumed
rate limits are per peer and per lane, and report the exact wait
a flood of forged requests cannot spend the real peer's allowance
a local stop runs first through a full ordinary queue and a remote peer's flood of priority commands
the local user keeps priority slots a remote flood cannot take, but the lane is still bounded
a peer revoked after its command was accepted has no effect, and can no longer read the outcome
rebinding a peer's key after acceptance also expires the commands accepted under the old binding
an accepted command that waits past its time limit expires unapplied, and that is its recorded outcome
cancel: before the commit it withdraws; after, across peers and against a stop it changes nothing
the local user is never refused for epoch or revision, but a remote controller in the same position is
priority is not an authentication bypass: a forged stop from the local user's identity is refused
a retry storm leaves the queue and the ledger bounded and produces one effect
a command naming a member the group does not have is refused with no effect, and the refusal is the recorded outcome
relative volume is resolved against the live value and clamped at both ends of 0..=100
a step applies at most its budget, priority first, and what is left waits for the next step
a command the session refuses for a reason that is not the sender's (another caller took the number) is an internal fault, recorded without detail; an unknown member is still the sender's
after a restart a late absolute copy and a late relative copy are refused, nothing is reverted, and a command composed after the restart is applied
a restarted channel starts its session numbers above everything it used before, so the first commands after a restart are not internal faults
absolute volume is naturally repeatable: commands composed against an older revision than the current one still apply within an incarnation
a remote controller's volume or mute names the revision it read, or is turned away at the door; a revision the session has not reached is refused; stop, cancel and the local user need none
with no group lease (a fresh or restarted channel) group-changing commands are refused before the session is touched, a local stop and mute-on still work, and the refusals are not recorded
a deposed leader's late command is refused after the issuer advances the epoch, and the same command is applied once the new epoch's lease is installed
an expired lease is refused at the instant it expires, and renewal plus resubmit is applied

a lease the session does not accept (foreign issuer, foreign group, stale, future, already expired) cannot be installed, a token with two flaws is refused for the first in G01's order (group, stale, future, issuer, expiry), and the lease already held keeps working
a forged request fails authentication before the lease is consulted; a genuine one reaches the lease check
a cancel needs no lease: it only withdraws its own sender's waiting work
